page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.large is an entry-tier virtual server instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 2 dedicated x86_64 virtual central processing units paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include integrated GPU hardware accelerators, nor does it include bundled local disk storage, requiring external network-attached volumes for data persistence.

The architecture provides dedicated CPU execution without shared-core throttling, though advanced instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, AMX, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions are not available in the guest environment. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are also omitted from the standard hardware allocation, requiring network infrastructure configuration for external reachability.

Given the balanced yet compute-skewed 1:2 resource allocation and lack of onboard storage, ecs.s2.large provides a lightweight compute profile. The configuration matches baseline infrastructure roles such as running lightweight web services, microservice APIs, background task workers, CI/CD utility nodes, and development environments that operate without intense memory requirements or specialized vector computation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.large is a KVM-virtualized cloud instance featuring 2 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory. Operating with a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core, this instance targets workloads requiring dedicated compute cycles with moderate memory overhead. The configuration provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for data persistence, and includes zero GPU accelerators. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the virtual machine. Advanced vector extensions and hardware cryptography instructions are unexposed. With dedicated CPU allocation, ecs.s2.large suits lightweight computational tasks, utility services, staging environments, API microservices, and general backend application serving where massive memory density and specialized instruction sets are not required.
